text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Scotiabank bids for National Trustco: Offer totals C$1.25-billion as Jackman agrees to unload his stake of 47 percent.
- Ottawa taking C$60-million stake in cancer drugs: Federal, Ontario lobbying wins C$350-million research program.
- Apparat cripples Ukraine reforms: Bureaucratic tail wags political dog.
- Leafs' arena plan crumbles as negotiations with city fail: Plan to share new facility with Raptors also appears doomed.
- Queen greets Matthew and crew: Thousands watch replica reach land.
- 'Final' proposal on salmon fails to move U.S. team: Rejection would send clear signal on real goal, B.C. says.
- Royal deal could top C$2 billion: London Insurance shares jump as owner Trilon, bank dicker over takeover's price.
- Hal Jackman finally can relax: The National Trustco chairman managed to keep the family trust company afloat - and independent - through some perilous times.
- Group bids for Anchor Lamina: Harrowston leads C$182-million offer for auto sector supplier.
- Scotiabank bids C$1.25 billion for National Trustco: Sector shakeup accelerates with swoop for one of the last remaining independent trusts.
- U.S. warns Bow Valley over Iranian project.
